title: Hosted data residency enforcement — PRD: completion, stakeholder review, and sign-off gates
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Track PRD completion + stakeholder review + sign-off gates for Hosted data residency enforcement (region pinning + deterministic enforcement + clear errors + auditability).

What we’re shipping (Phase 1 scope)
1) Region pinning configuration
- Allow org/project (and optionally API key) to declare:
  - allowed_regions: set of regions (e.g., ["eu-west", "eu-central"])
  - primary_region: single region used when multiple allowed
  - allow_cross_region_fallback: default false (explicit opt-in only)
- Precedence: API key policy overrides project overrides org (unless explicitly disabled; see Open Questions).

2) Enforcement
- Guarantee request routing + fallback behavior respects allowed region set.
- Block any cross-region attempt deterministically at request time.
- Ensure background processing, logs, traces, and operational tooling do not move customer content outside pinned region(s), per ADR-021.

3) Error contract
- Standardized HTTP status + machine-readable error_code + request_id + actionable message.
- Must be consistent across streaming and non-streaming endpoints.
- SDKs surface a dedicated exception type with error_code + help_url.

4) Observability + auditability
- Residency decision logs: policy evaluated, selected region, block reason.
- Metrics/dashboards: blocked requests, eval latency, cross-region attempt counters.
- Audit log events for create/update/delete residency policies and any admin override.

Non-goals (for initial release)
- Automatic multi-region replication of customer content.
- Bespoke residency rules for every internal subsystem beyond enforcement boundaries captured in ADR-021; remaining hardening tracked as follow-ups.

Success metrics (first 30 days post-GA)
- 0 confirmed incidents of customer content leaving pinned region due to routing/fallback.
- <0.5% false-positive block rate for allowlisted customers during rollout (measured as blocks reversed by config correction or acknowledged product bug).
- 100% of residency blocks return standardized error payload across endpoints (including streaming).
- Audit log coverage: 100% of residency policy changes recorded and exportable.

Rollout plan (as reflected in PRD)
- Phase 0: discovery + threat model + customer input aggregation.
- Phase 1: ship core pinning + enforcement + error contract + observability.
- Phase 2+: harden edge systems (as needed) and extend coverage (e.g., richer per-service guardrails) based on evidence/learned failure modes.

Primary stakeholders for sign-off
- Product: Naomi Feldman
- Program: Talia Benson
- Security: Marcus Lin; executive sponsor Dr. Aisha Rahman
- GRC: Olga Petrov (evidence requirements)
- Eng: Ethan Park (control plane), Mina Haddad + Ravi Menon (routing), Amara Diallo (gateway)
- SRE: Sean Gallagher + Rafael Mendes
- Docs/Enablement: Elliot Price, Wei Chen, Kira Thompson

Notes
This Linear ticket is the PRD tracking umbrella and sign-off gate. Engineering execution is tracked in ENG/DES tickets linked above; error messaging product requirements tracked in PM-1490.
acceptance_criteria:
PRD acceptance criteria
- PRD published in Confluence and linked in this ticket.
- Requirements are concrete and testable:
  - Policy objects and precedence rules documented.
  - Enforcement boundaries and definition of “customer content” aligned with ADR-021.
  - Error contract aligned with ADR-022, including streaming behavior.
  - Observability/audit requirements include specific events/fields.
- Rollout plan includes:
  - Allowlist strategy + feature flag plan.
  - SRE monitoring + paging thresholds.
  - Customer communication plan for allowlisted beta.
- Explicit non-goals and phased hardening plan captured.
- Open questions section includes owner + target decision date + current decision.

Sign-off acceptance criteria
- Product sign-off: Naomi Feldman
- Security sign-off: Marcus Lin + Dr. Aisha Rahman
- SRE sign-off: Sean Gallagher
- GRC sign-off (evidence readiness): Olga Petrov
- Eng leads acknowledge feasibility and sequencing: Ethan Park, Mina Haddad, Amara Diallo

Exit criteria for this ticket
- All required sign-offs recorded in this ticket’s updates.
- Follow-up issues created for any deferred decisions or phase-2 items.
open_questions:
Q1: Policy precedence defaults — should API key residency policy be allowed to override a stricter org/project policy?
Owner: Naomi Feldman + Marcus Lin
Decision: API key can only be stricter or equal; cannot broaden allowed_regions beyond org/project (documented in PRD v1.3).

Q2: What identifiers can we safely return in public error payloads (policy_id vs policy_name)?
Owner: Brian Murphy + Marcus Lin
Decision: Return policy_id (opaque UUID) and a short help_url; do not return free-form policy name (to avoid leaking internal naming).

Q3: Which HTTP status code for residency blocks?
Owner: Naomi Feldman + Amara Diallo
Decision: 409 Conflict (aligned with ADR-022).

Q4: Dedicated alignment — do we support the same residency policy objects for Dedicated capacity?
Owner: Naomi Feldman + Mina Haddad
Decision: Dedicated uses its own capacity-region constraints; PRD states “aligned behavior where applicable,” but Hosted residency policies are not automatically applied to Dedicated unless customer opts in via contract/config (tracked as Phase 2 follow-up).

Q5: Logging/tracing — what cross-region metadata is allowed?
Owner: Ravi Menon + Logan Wright
Decision: Allowed cross-region metadata is limited to non-content operational metrics and request identifiers per ADR-021; no prompts/completions/token logs outside region.

Q6: Background jobs (abuse detection, rate limit analytics) — do any pipelines process request content cross-region today?
Owner: Sean Gallagher + Logan Wright
Decision: No content pipelines permitted; current jobs audited and updated to ensure content stays regionalized. Any exception requires security approval + explicit PRD addendum.
